subject.title: Skill and Read tools truncating output at ~600-700 chars in 2026.6.11

question: Should maintainers require a live packaged-gateway reproduction of the reported 600-700 character cutoff and Skill Workshop proposal lookup failure before authorizing a code fix?
rationale: The source-backed caps on current main and v2026.6.11 are much higher than the reported cutoff, and the remaining plausible causes span rendering, transcript/model context, provider transport, and workspace-scoped proposal lookup.

options.title: Require Live Repro First
options.body: Keep the issue open and ask for or run a packaged Linux gateway repro with transcript and workspace-state evidence before changing caps or persistence logic.

options.title: Start Source Investigation Now
options.body: Assign a maintainer to trace downstream display, transcript, embedded-runner, and Skill Workshop state paths without waiting for reporter proof, accepting higher risk of chasing the wrong layer.

options.title: Split The Report
options.body: Track read-tool-only truncation under the older read-output issue and require a separate Skill Workshop state report if live evidence shows a distinct root cause.

recommendation.title: Require Live Repro First
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and ask for or run a packaged Linux gateway repro with transcript and workspace-state evidence before changing caps or persistence logic.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus is the strongest recent history signal for aggregate tool-result truncation, which is the most plausible shared layer for multi-tool output symptoms after per-tool caps did not match.
